catalog_quote: Il y a deux éléments tonaux opposés en kpele: haut H et bas B. ... Phonologiquement, le kpele a aussi un ton haut flottant écrit entre parenthèses (H). ... Les tons ont une valeur contrastive au niveau du lexique : láa /láá/ ‘coucher’ – làa /làà/ ‘là-bas’, kpâŋ /kpáŋ̀/ ‘gris-gris contre le vol’ – kpàŋ /kpàŋ̀/ ‘chaume’, kálaŋ /káláŋ́/ ‘plaque’ – kálâŋ /káláŋ̀/ ‘épaule’ – kàlâŋ /kàláŋ̀/ ‘religion’ ... Les tons ont également une valeur grammaticale. ... 3.1. Mélodies tonales. Au niveau des mots, qui ont une structure mono- ou disyllabique dans la plupart des cas, les tons forment des séquences fixes, dites mélodies tonales. Les six séquences tonales principales sont /H/, /HB/, /BHB/, /B(H)/, /B/, /BH/ ... [Konoshenko & Uvarova 2025:] Guinean Kpelle is a tone language featuring a binary L vs. H contrast. The tonal elements make up fixed melodies, e.g., the most common are /H/, /L H /, /HL/,…

Есть лексический плавающий высокий тон, который всегда следует за низким и обозначается гачеком на конечном гласном слова: yàlǎ ‛лев’ [...] Контурный тон представляет собой сочетание двух фонологически уровневых. [p. 287:] Сегментная база тона в ГК — гласный. Тоны в ГК образуют фиксированные последовательности (мелодии). Сегментная база тональных последовательностей — с т о п а (см. 2.2.1.). Непроизводные морфемы группируются в 6 тональных классов, из которых 6-й является наименее частотным.
new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Phonological stress is absent in GK [Guinean Kpelle]. There are two level tones: H (high) and L (low). There is a lexical floating high tone, which always follows a low tone and is marked with a háček on the final vowel of the word: yàlǎ 'lion' [...] A contour tone is a combination of two phonologically level tones. [p. 287:] The segmental base of tone in GK is the vowel. Tones in GK form fixed sequences (melodies). The segmental base of tonal sequences is the foot (see 2.2.1). Non-derived morphemes are grouped into 6 tonal classes, of which the 6th is the least frequent.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record (classification tonal-OR-pitch accent from Konoshenko 2019/2008 and Konoshenko & Uvarova 2025) notes those sources are silent on stress ('No word-stress rule stated anywhere'). This chapter is compatible (same binary H/L system, floating H, the same six melodies) and adds the explicit statement that phonological stress is absent, which upgrades 'silent on stress' to an explicit no-word-stress claim and names the melody domain (the foot).
new_statements.rule_in_words: The source states outright that Guinean Kpelle has no phonological stress. Word prosody is tonal: two level tones H and L plus a lexical floating H (always after L, written on the word-final vowel), organized into six fixed lexical melodies /H/, /L(H)/, /HL/, /LHL/, /L/, /LH/ whose domain is the 'foot' (стопа, §2.2.1, p. 290), a cohesion unit defined by vowel co-occurrence restrictions, nasal harmony, consonant distribution and fixed tone melodies, not by any prominence peak. Grammatical replacive melodies /L/ and /L(H)/ also exist (pp. 287-288).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not applicable; nothing on secondary stress or any prominence (no stress at all per the source).
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. Tonal notes: the Tongonaaloi subdialect has a marginal mid tone (contextual on verbs, lexical in a few function words and in CVCVCV(V) nouns; p. 286-287); /LH/ melody is marginal and cannot surface on CVV in the Honkwele subdialect described (p. 291, §2.2.1); /L(H)/ vs /L/ neutralize before a high tone (p. 287, note 3).
new_statements.identity_note: Konoshenko 2017 states (p. 285, §2.0.0) that it describes central Guinean Kpelle, specifically the Honkwele (хонквеле) subdialect spoken in Nzérékoré, with material from the Tongonaaloi (тонгонаалой) subdialect and the northern Gbali (гбали) dialect flagged where used; the no-stress statement is made for 'ГК' (Guinean Kpelle) generally. Konoshenko & Khachaturyan 2024 concerns Guinean Kpelle (Guerzé, iso gkp) of Forest Guinea as the contact language of Mano; its main object is Mano final lowering, with Kpelle L1 speakers as a baseline. Neither work covers Liberian Kpelle (libe1247).
